journal_name: Studies in English Language and Education
title: Overall English learning satisfaction in vocational education: A gendered and disciplinary perspective
abstract: The challenges that the students in China’s higher vocational colleges encounter when learning English negatively influence their Overall English Learning Satisfaction (OELS) in the College English Course (CEC). Although substantial studies have examined satisfaction with English learning, most have focused on general higher education contexts. As a result, English learning satisfaction in CEC in higher vocational institutions has received comparatively less attention, particularly regarding disciplinary and gender differences. In response, the present study investigated students’ satisfaction using a questionnaire mainly adapted from the China Customer Satisfaction Index. Data were collected using a 16-item, five-point Likert-scale survey within 1,057 non-English major students across three vocational colleges in Zhuhai, Guangdong Province. The group differences were analyzed through the independent-samples t-test, Welch’s analysis, and the Gaines-Howell post-hoc test. The results indicated that the overall OELS level of the students was moderate to high, with significant gender and discipline differences. journal_name: Studies in English Language and Education
title: Integrating local culture-based gamification to enhance EFL reading literacy in elementary education
abstract: Reading literacy is crucial for EFL learners. Nevertheless, elementary school students often struggle to comprehend English texts because they lack meaningful, contextually appropriate learning experiences. Although gamification has been used extensively to increase students’ participation and learning achievement, little empirical research has examined the integration of local culture into gamified EFL reading instruction at the elementary school level. This study examined the effectiveness of local culture-based gamification in enhancing EFL students’ reading literacy in terms of achievement, engagement, and motivation. Two Grade VI students in an Indonesian elementary school participated in this quasi-experimental pretest-posttest control group design. The control group received conventional reading instruction, while the experimental group received reading instruction through local culture-based gamification. A validated EFL reading literacy exam, an engagement observation rubric, and a learning motivation questionnaire were used to collect data. journal_name: Studies in English Language and Education
title: EFL pre-service teachers’ AI literacy and metacognitive awareness in English language teaching
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly reshaping English language teaching (ELT) and engaging with AI in pedagogically meaningful, ethical, and reflective ways. This study investigates English as foreign language (EFL) pre-service teachers’ perspectives on AI literacy and metacognitive awareness (MA) in the context of ELT. It explores how they understand and use AI tools in pedagogical practice. A mixed methods approach was employed, involving a survey of 225 respondents who completed the online questionnaire via Google Forms and a semi-structured interview with 20 participants to gain comprehensive insights into their perceptions and experiences. The quantitative findings reveal strong agreement that AI plays a role in providing flexible, effective, efficient, and personalized learning. However, neutral stances were highlighted regarding their understanding of different types of AI tools and their ability to distinguish between generative and non-generative AI, indicating a gap in their AI literacy. journal_name: Studies in English Language and Education
title: The role of AI in reducing reading anxiety and enhancing ambiguity tolerance among EFL students
abstract: This quasi-experimental mixed-methods study investigated the effects of AI-assisted reading instruction on foreign language reading anxiety and ambiguity tolerance among university-level EFL learners. Drawing on Cognitive Load Theory, Attentional Control Theory, and Positive Psychology, the study examined whether structured use of GPT-4–based text simplification and feedback mechanisms could alleviate affective barriers while enhancing cognitive flexibility in reading. A total of 120 intermediate EFL students were assigned to experimental (n = 60) and control (n = 60) groups over a 12-week intervention. The experimental group engaged in AI-supported reading sessions involving adaptive text simplification, contextual clarification, and immediate formative feedback, while the control group received traditional instruction. Quantitative data were collected using the Foreign Language Reading Anxiety Scale (FLRAS) and the Second Language Ambiguity Tolerance Scale (SLATS), complemented by semi-structured interviews. journal_name: Studies in English Language and Education
title: Demystifying religious advice in Indonesian public signage: Hybridity of linguistic landscape and translation studies
abstract: The study aimed to examine religious messages on public signs in Parepare City, South Sulawesi, Indonesia, from the perspectives of linguistic landscape and translation studies. The research focused on a corpus of public religious signs collected from several major areas of Parepare. It employed a qualitative approach by adopting an observational research design and visual documentation through photography. This study revealed that religious messages displayed on public billboards reflect a universal Islamic ideology, which can be categorized into themes of monotheism (tauhid), Islamic law (sharia), and morality. In analyzing the Indonesian renderings of Arabic expressions, the present study applied the translation techniques framework proposed by Molina and Albir, identifying the use of established equivalence, compensation, reduction, modulation, amplification, borrowing, and transposition. The use of these techniques contributes to the achievement of high-quality translations. journal_name: Studies in English Language and Education
title: Linguistic signalling of rhetorical segmentation in academic introductions: Empirical extension of the CaRS model
abstract: Research on academic writing has long described the rhetorical structure of research article introductions through Swales’ Create-a-Research-Space (CaRS) model. However, the question of whether rhetorical segmentation is systematically realised in surface linguistic form remains underexamined. The present study provides empirical evidence that rhetorical segmentation in academic introductions is reflected in the distribution of sentence-initial expressions. The analysis is based on the CaRS-50 corpus, comprising fifty research article introductions annotated at sentence level for Moves and Steps. Sentence-initial spans up to the first comma were extracted automatically and examined in relation to sequential Move transitions. Across 1,297 sentences, 36.4% begin with an identifiable opener, while 21.5% of adjacent sentence pairs involve a Move change, establishing a corpus-level baseline transition probability. Recurrent openers were evaluated relative to this baseline. journal_name: Studies in English Language and Education
title: Intonation as a prosodic characteristic of the Deli Malay language
abstract: Medan City (MC) is a multicultural city. The language use in MC is characterized by distinctive intonational patterns commonly perceived as harsh, which function as markers of local speech identity. This prosodic profile contrasts with the traditionally softer intonation of Deli Malay (DM), the region’s indigenous language, suggesting ongoing prosodic shift under conditions of language contact. This study investigates the intonation phrase patterns of DM to document its prosodic structure and examine its use within the multilingual context of MC. Employing an experimental acoustic-phonetic approach, speech data from 10 native DM speakers aged over 50 were analyzed in Praat using the Autosegmental-Metrical (AM) framework. Pre-arranged 50 target sentences representing declarative, informative interrogative, confirmatory interrogative, and imperative modes were elicited. The findings reveal a two-tone intonational system organized around low (L) and high (H*) tonal events. journal_name: Studies in English Language and Education
title: Integrating Canva AI-driven worksheet design into Environmental Project-Based English Learning for young learners
abstract: This study explores the integration of AI-driven Canva in designing English for young learners (EYL) worksheets, framed within Environmental Project-Based English Learning (EPjBEL) and the deep learning paradigm mandated by Indonesian Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education to promote mindful, meaningful, and joyful learning based on eight dimensions of learner profiles. Meanwhile, existing EYL materials, such as textbook-based exercises, often lack real-world relevance and fail to engage learners in deep, meaningful, continuous learning experiences that are linguistically rich and environmentally relevant. Through a classroom-based research design, the study involved 63 Indonesian pre-service EYL teachers who utilized Canva’s AI features and other digital tools to create environmental project-based English worksheets. The data collection methods included classroom observations, semi-structured interviews, questionnaires, document analysis, and reflective journals. The findings revealed that the participants effectively used Canva’s AI-driven features to create visually engaging, pedagogically sound materials that promote environmental awareness. journal_name: Studies in English Language and Education
title: Second language online assessment practices: What L2 teachers think, do, and feel
abstract: The digital transformation of education has revolutionized second language (L2) writing, reshaping how students compose texts and how teachers assess writing and develop assessment literacy. However, existing research has provided an incomplete picture of what university L2 writing teachers in the Philippines thought, did, and felt when assessments were conducted in fully online learning spaces. Addressing this gap, this study explored how L2 writing teachers understood, enacted, and managed online assessment within the conceptual, praxeological, and socio-emotional dimensions of teachers’ assessment literacy. Using a case study design, semi-structured interviews were conducted with nine university L2 writing teachers, and the multilevel coding method was employed to enable close analysis of their assessment reasoning, enacted strategies, and experienced pressures. The findings showed that within the conceptual dimension, teachers largely viewed online assessment as a continuation of traditional goals while adapting to digital environments. journal_name: Studies in English Language and Education
title: Grammatical metaphor and writing quality: A Systemic Functional Linguistics approach to EFL university students’ argumentative prose
abstract: One indicator that students are beginning to write more academically is their shift from everyday wording to more compressed and abstract forms of expression. This study examines how grammatical metaphor (GM) relates to the quality of academic writing among university EFL students. Within Systemic Functional Linguistics, this study analyzes ideational and interpersonal GM in a corpus of 120 argumentative essays (≈75,000 words) written by intermediate (CEFR B2) undergraduates. Using a mixed-methods, corpus-based correlational design, GM frequency was normalized per 1,000 words and compared with holistic writing scores (κ = .85 for inter-rater reliability).
